title: Fit quality is not identifiability: a harmonized robustness, integration-value and calibration audit of groundwater inference under data limitation
scope: A companion benchmark article to M2.3 (the HydroSheaf framework paper) and sibling to O3 (Objective 3). O4 does not introduce new software architecture. It harmonizes three already-locked, independently designed component benchmarks (M6 field-transfer/robustness, M7 conditional-integration/non-identifiability, M8 calibration-is-not-identification) under one taxonomy and reports a cross-component pattern no single component paper can show alone: under data limitation, evidence misspecification, or a model-form shift, an internally-generated confidence signal (fit quality, posterior-entropy reduction, nominal interval coverage, optimiser convergence) can remain stable or favourable while an externally-verifiable truth signal (true identifiability class, independent-generator predictive skill, realised parameter-recovery error, structural information rank) degrades or diverges.

objectives.statement: Harmonize M6, M7 and M8's independently designed stress tests (data-limitation tier ablation, evidence misspecification/adverse controls, model-form shift to independent numerical truth) into one common taxonomy of internal-signal versus external-signal pairs.
acceptance_criteria: A taxonomy table classifies every retained M6/M7/M8 experiment cited by stress axis and by whether a paired internal/external signal is reported.
No experiment is re-labelled in a way that contradicts its component DECISIONS.md.

objectives.statement: Quantify, for each of the three layers, how an internally-generated confidence signal behaves relative to an externally-verifiable truth signal as stress increases.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-component comparison figure and table report the internal and external signal side by side for M6, M7 and M8 using each component's own locked headline metric.
Every reported value traces to a primary CSV/JSON artefact under M6/M7/M8 results/ directories or M8's registered manuscript tables, with no recomputation of the underlying inference.

objectives.statement: Report the negative and structural controls that bound each layer's central finding, so the divergence pattern is shown to be a property of the stress test and not an artefact of the classifier or reporting convention.
acceptance_criteria: Table reports each layer's negative/structural control result alongside its main finding.

objectives.statement: Compare the three benchmarks on design/computational scale (replicate counts, case counts, bootstrap resamples) and on field-/archive-transfer scope, disclosing that this scope is uneven across layers (M8 has none).
acceptance_criteria: A benchmark-scale table reports replicate/case/bootstrap counts and transfer scope for all three components from their own manifests.

objectives.statement: Describe, for a reader unfamiliar with the project, every dataset (synthetic and field) that any of the three benchmarks consumes, at a level sufficient to reproduce the comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Data section and a data-inventory table cover the Northern Ghana/Talensi/Lower Anayari field datasets, the independent MODFLOW 6/MODPATH 7 generator used by M7, and the controlled-synthetic transport/kinetic/topology designs used by M8, each with source, size, and role.

inputs.provenance: M6 locked field-transfer/robustness benchmark result tables (Northern Ghana/Talensi/Lower Anayari, five-tier evidence ablation, synthetic validation with known truth, evidence-gate-off negative control)

M7 locked conditional-integration benchmark result tables (m7_3_locked native/adverse-control contrasts; RUN-M7-SHEAF-VS-GRAPH-20260729-01; RUN-M7-ROBUST-HYBRID-SHEAF-20260729-01; RUN-M7-6-M3-MECHANISM-20260731-01)

M8 locked calibration benchmark result tables (fixed-design sweep, optimal-design experiment, kinetic structural control, independent-model robustness, active-learning portability and frontier qualification); cross-checked against M8/m8_calibration_benchmark/manuscript/Manuscript-Final.md's own registered tables
M2.3 recomputed evidence exports, read only for cross-checking consistency with the companion framework paper, not as a primary evidence source for O4

risks.risk: Overlap/self-plagiarism against O3, which harmonizes the sibling M3/M4/M5 triad under a different axis.
risks.mitigation: O4 asks a disjoint question (internal-signal vs external-signal divergence under stress, not capture vs correctness under independent evaluation) of a disjoint evidence set; Discussion states the relationship to O3 and M2.3 explicitly.

risks.risk: M6/M7/M8 locked results predate the 2026-08-01/02 hydrosheaf/validation programme-layer changes.
risks.mitigation: Verified by tracing the actual per-script import graph of every M6/M7/M8 script producing a cited number against the literal diff of every changed shared module, not only by module-dependency reasoning; three headline numbers were independently recomputed from raw CSVs and matched their prose summaries exactly; the one stale number chain found (M7 public-pipeline system-acceptance run) is excluded from every claim. Full detail in DECISIONS.md D3.

risks.risk: Re-deriving cross-component numbers could silently diverge from each component's own locked, reviewed values.
risks.mitigation: Python synthesis layer reads only already-locked CSV/JSON artefacts and performs no re-simulation; every derived number is cross-checked against the value quoted in the component's own docs/*_results.md or manuscript tables.

risks.risk: M8 has no field-transfer component, unlike M6, which could be read as inconsistent scope.
risks.mitigation: This asymmetry is stated directly in Results/Discussion and in the benchmark-scale table (TAB-4) rather than smoothed over or implied to be equivalent.
